The Sentinelese are never quoted, never explained, never made monsters: it is their home.

entries.title: Washed up
entries.text:
The storm put me on the reef before dawn and the surf did the rest. The dinghy is holed but whole. I have my flashlight, my clothes, salt in everything.
I know whose island this is. Everyone does. I did not mean to land here, and that will not matter to anyone watching from the trees.

entries.title: The Missionary's camp
entries.text:
A red kayak lies overturned above the tide line, split along the keel. Two arrows stand in the trunk of the palm over it, high up, fletched with something pale. They were never meant to hit anyone.
Under the kayak: a coil of orange cord, a folded tarp, and a plastic bag holding a swollen notebook. What is left of him lies further up, under the palms. I leave him as he is.

entries.title: The Missionary's notebook
entries.text:
3 Mar. Landed on the south beach at first light. I have rehearsed what I will say a hundred times, knowing they will not understand a word. That is not the point. The point is to come in peace and be seen to.
4 Mar. They came out of the trees shouting, and two arrows went into the palm above me. Above me, not at me. I paddled out, and I came back. A man who keeps coming back, unarmed, must in the end be let in.
6 Mar. The man in the mangroves says the arrows mean go back. He says it kindly. He does not understand what I am here for.
9 Mar. Sat on the sand all morning with my hands open. Nobody came, though I think they watched. I am less sure than I was of what I have to give them.
11 Mar. If this book is found, do not blame them. I came uninvited. They have told me as plainly as anyone can that this is their home.

entries.title: The Freighter Sailor
entries.text:
Where the mangroves give way to forest, the roots have grown through an orange life vest, the old kind with the stiff collar. The bones inside it are long since clean.
A crowbar lies across his knees, as if he had been holding it when he sat down for the last time. Beside him, a dented tin flask with words scratched into its side, and a folded page sealed in plastic.

entries.title: Scratched on the flask
entries.text:
MV CELANDINE. ASHORE FOR WATER. BOAT DID NOT COME BACK FOR ME.
AFT CABIN HATCH JAMMED WHEN SHE HEELED. BAR OPENS IT.
BATTERY + FLARE LOCKER BELOW. LOW WATER ONLY.
THEY WATCH THE REEF.

entries.title: A page of the Celandine's log
entries.text:
0340. Grounded on the reef in heavy weather. Heavy list to port. No injuries. Master orders all hands to remain aboard pending rescue.
Radio room flooded to the sill; main set dead. Spare battery and pyrotechnics locker are in the aft cabin. Cabin hatch jammed by the list. Bosun to work it free with the bar when the sea allows.
Water ration halved. Shore party to look for a spring at low water.

entries.title: The Rogue Cartographer's camp
entries.text:
A dome tent of the nineties kind, green and grey, folded in on itself under a fallen branch. A satellite phone with a stub aerial, screen black, battery swollen. Survey pegs in a neat row. A pouch of signal flares wrapped in waxed cloth, still dry.
Beyond the camp, on the face of a black stone, a map, nailed at the corners. Faded, but careful.

entries.title: The map on the stone
entries.text:
His map is better than anything I could draw. The reef and the wreck, with tide times pencilled beside them. A high point in the north-west, marked SIGNAL? Springs, ringed in blue. A gap in the southern reef: BOAT PASSAGE, HIGH WATER ONLY. In the western mangroves, a small square and a question: someone lives here?
Across the middle he drew nothing at all, only the stones, and over them, in a hand that is not quite steady: DO NOT TRUST THE PATH BEHIND YOU.
I copy what I can into my own map.

entries.title: The Cartographer's field book
entries.text:
Day 1. Phone dead on arrival. Moisture? Compass fine. Base camp in the clearing. Begin the traverse tomorrow.
Day 2. Compass useless within two kilometres of the centre. Not magnetic deviation: it does not point anywhere, it wanders. Reverted to pacing and sun sights.
Day 5. Paths re-walked today do not match yesterday's. Error in my pacing? Checked twice. They do not match.
Day 6. The islanders set posts on their beaches. Driftwood, lashed with cord, a shell or a bone at the crown. Near them the hum is lower. Made one of my own and carried it. It works. I do not know why it works.
Day 9. The hum is in the instruments and in me. I have named the centre the Quiet Meridian. It should be measured. It must be measured.
Day ? the map is on the stone where it will not move. the paths move. the stone does not. going in for the last bearing

entries.title: What Marek told me
entries.text:
Two things to remember, he said.
The reef in the north-east can be walked to the wreck at low water. At high water it takes you, and gives nothing back.
And metal: anything that hums, or clicks, or shines. Near their paths, put it away. He does not know whether it is the people or the island that hates it. He stopped trying to tell.

entries.title: The sailor's bar
entries.text:
The wreck's cabin is sealed, rusted shut, and the hatch is heavy.
The sailor from the freighter carried a pry bar for the hatches. Always, even asleep. Marek says he lies in the roots where the mangroves meet the forest, south-east of the shack.

entries.title: Driftwood totem
entries.text:
Driftwood from the shore, a length of cord, and a bone or a shell, lashed in a cross and carried.
The islanders set posts like this at the borders of their beaches. Near them, the hum is lower. Not gone. Lower.

entries.title: Patching the dinghy
entries.text:
The tarp over the split, folded twice and lashed around the hull with cord; a length of driftwood braced across inside to hold the shape.
It will not be pretty. It only has to float as far as the passage, and a long way past it.

entries.title: The dinghy
entries.text:
Grey rubber, one chamber split along a seam, the floor still sound. With a tarp across the split, cord to lash it and a length of wood to hold the shape, it would float.
It would have to wait for high water to get over the reef.

entries.title: The cabin hatch
entries.text: A steel hatch on the wreck's after deck, rusted into its frame. I put my whole weight on the wheel and it did not move at all. It will need a bar, and low water to reach it.

entries.title: Inside the Celandine
entries.text:
The bar went in under the lip and the hatch gave with a shriek I felt in my teeth. Anyone within a long way heard it too.
Below: a small cabin, half dark. A locker with an orange flare pistol, one cartridge already in it. A marine battery in a sealed case, its switch left on all these years. Cord, and a tarp still in its wrapping. Someone packed this cabin for exactly this. Nobody came to use it.

entries.title: The radio rock
entries.text:
A slab of rock at the top of the ridge, flat as a table. Someone has been up here before me: a rusted bracket bolted into the stone, a few strands of old wire.
From here a flare would be seen from the sea. From everywhere on the island too.

entries.title: A shack in the mud
entries.text: A shack on stilts in the mangroves, roofed with palm and tin gone brown. Smoke, and a net drying. Someone lives here, and has for a long time.

entries.title: The reef
entries.text: From here the reef runs out north-east towards the wreck. At low water it is a road of rock and pools. I watched the sea come back over it in the time it took to drink. Not a place to be caught.

entries.title: The wreck
entries.text: A freighter on her side on the reef, rust bleeding down the hull. The name is still legible on the bow: CELANDINE. The deck stays dry above the tide. Somewhere below it is a cabin.

entries.title: The stones
entries.text: Black stones standing in a ring, taller than a man and smooth, as if worked. No birds. The compass needle will not settle. I could feel the hum in my teeth before I saw them.

entries.title: Signal Peak
entries.text: The top of the ridge. Bare rock, and the whole sea to the north and west. Anyone out there would see a light from here. Anyone on the island would see it too.

entries.title: The passage
entries.text: A gap in the outer reef, darker water between the breakers. At high tide a small boat could get through here. At low tide it would tear its bottom out.

entries.title: Fishers' camp
entries.text: Fire-blackened stones, fish bones, a rack of split cane for drying. Recent. Whoever fishes here comes and goes with the tide, and I am standing in their place. Among the stones, a sealed field dressing the sea brought from somewhere else. I take what was washed up and leave the rack alone.

entries.title: Collapsed hut
entries.text: A lean-to of poles and thatch, fallen in on itself years ago. Inside, a canvas satchel rotted through and a first-aid tin with a ship's stamp. Not theirs. Somebody else waited here once.

entries.title: Old shrine
entries.text:
Stones set in a low ring, shells laid along the top, and at the centre a post of driftwood lashed with cord, a shell bound at its crown. The air is quieter here.
I do not touch the post, but I look at it long enough to see how it is made. A few shells have rolled out of the ring into the grass.

entries.title: Hunters' blind
entries.text: A screen of woven fronds facing a game trail, old and still sound. Someone sits here for hours without moving. I should learn to do the same.

entries.title: Bone pit
entries.text: A hollow full of pig bones, old kills cleaned by ants and rain. Not a grave. A larder's leftovers, and a sign of how long people have lived well here.

entries.title: Stone cairn
entries.text: A heap of stones taller than me, built with care and old enough for moss. A marker, I think, though I cannot say of what. The trail bends round it and never crosses.

entries.title: Old lookout
entries.text: A shelf of rock above the east beach, worn smooth where people have sat. From here you see every boat that could come. They are still watching for one.

entries.title: The tide
entries.text: Low water opens the reef to the wreck. Be off it before the turn.

entries.title: Metal
entries.text: Near their paths, keep metal stowed and switch off anything that hums.

entries.title: Warnings
entries.text: An arrow in the sand at my feet means go back. So I go back.

entries.title: The mud
entries.text: They do not come into the mud round Marek's shack. There, I can sit.

entries.title: The totem
entries.text: A driftwood totem, carried, quiets the hum. It does not silence it.

entries.title: The battery
entries.text: The radio battery hums while it is switched on. Off, unless I need it.

entries.title: The flare
entries.text: The flare goes up from the peak and nowhere else, where a ship could see it.

entries.title: High water
entries.text: A boat goes out on the high water, over the outer reef, never through it.
